sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Layout rules for grouped controls
sections.what: Sets the row or column layout and squares off the inner corners so the joined items read as one piece. It also removes the extra border between neighbors.
sections.why: Makes several controls look like a single control.
sections.watch_out: The rules target children by marker, so a child without the marker will not get the joined look.

sections.name: ButtonGroup
sections.title: Group container
sections.what: Draws the container that holds the controls. It announces itself as a group to screen readers and applies the chosen row or column layout.
sections.why: Groups related controls and gives screen readers their relationship.
sections.watch_out: Only horizontal and vertical layouts are defined, so any other value falls back to the base layout.

sections.name: ButtonGroupText
sections.title: Static label inside a group
sections.what: Draws a non-clickable piece of text or an icon styled like a button, for labeling part of a group such as a unit or a currency. It can be drawn as another element if the page asks.
sections.why: Lets a group carry a label next to its controls.
sections.watch_out: It is not a button, so clicking does nothing, and a label that looks clickable can confuse users.

sections.name: ButtonGroupSeparator
sections.title: Divider between items
sections.what: Draws a thin dividing line between grouped items. It is vertical by default.
sections.why: Separates items without adding a border to each one.
sections.watch_out: Because the default is vertical, a horizontal divider inside a vertical group must have its orientation set by the page.

summary: A container that joins several buttons, inputs or labels into one connected control.
purpose: Lets several related controls sit together in a row or column with shared edges and dividers.
why: Likely reason: makes a set of related controls look like one unit. Reason not stated in the code.
how: Step 1: Defines the row and column layout rules that square off the inner corners. Step 2: Builds the container with a group label for screen readers. Step 3: Builds a static label piece styled like a button. Step 4: Builds a thin divider line between items. Step 5: Makes all parts available to other files.
inputs: Buttons, inputs or labels placed inside, an orientation of horizontal or vertical, and extra style classes.
outputs: A joined row or column of controls on screen.
risks: The joined-edge rules target children by specific markers, so a child without the expected marker will not get joined edges.
debug: If corners look wrong, check the children's markers and the orientation value. If a divider looks wrong, check its orientation setting against the group layout.
